cross_modal_consistency.dimension_interpretation: The partition structural screen provides triage evidence on internal subdivision and boundary affinity in the candidate-generation consensus geometry. For both current sets, the dominant spectral gap is at the single-cluster resolution (candidate_eigengap 0.5724 for K3_C0001_M_K3_C0002 and 0.9572 for K3_C0003, both with screen_candidate_k=1), and the eigengap profiles show no dominant multi-cluster resolution. This means the screening calculation does not show a dominant internal subdivision signal for either set; it does not establish that the sets are internally homogeneous or independent. Within-set mean affinities are 0.3939 (n=75) and 0.6797 (n=28), while the nearest-pair between-set affinity is 0.2276, lower than both within-set values, indicating the current boundary is the relatively weakest link in this consensus geometry. These are partition-level structural diagnostics only; they do not by themselves establish biological meaning, clinical validity, or a decision to retain, split, or merge.

RNA shows a small positive mean silhouette (0.0619) with 29% negative patients, while CT, WSI, and WXS all show mean silhouettes near zero or slightly negative (CT -0.0049, WSI -0.0090, WXS -0.0045) with substantial negative fractions (CT 51%, WSI 65%, WXS 48%). The within-versus-between distance contrasts are correspondingly minimal in CT, WSI, and WXS. Synthesizing jointly rather than by vote counting, the overall native-view pattern provides weak and largely non-coherent geometric support for the current pair boundary, with RNA the only view showing any positive distinction. This addresses boundary representation only and does not itself determine whether the pair should be merged.

cross_modal_consistency.dimension_interpretation: In the candidate-generation consensus geometry, the current pair boundary between K3_C0001_M_K3_C0002 and K3_C0003 shows a mixed structural picture. The current boundary is only partially reproduced by an independent two-way spectral partition (ARI 0.581), and the normalized-cut cost is moderate-to-high (0.661), indicating appreciable cross-boundary connectivity rather than clean separation. Within-side affinity (0.428) exceeds between-side affinity (0.228) by roughly a factor of two, so the boundary is the relatively weaker link, but the contrast is moderate. Critically, the union of the two sets is dominated by the single-cluster resolution (candidate_eigengap 0.546 at candidate_k=1, with much smaller subsequent eigengaps), which is merge-compatible evidence and must not be interpreted as support for preserving the current two-set boundary. Taken jointly, the pattern is conflicting-to-weak: a partially represented current boundary coexisting with a single-cluster-dominated union. This is a coherent merge-compatible structural pattern, but it is not by itself sufficient to mandate any action. These are partition-level structural diagnostics only and do not establish biological meaning or clinical validity.

The single-cluster-dominated union here aligns with the merge-compatible reading of that weak boundary representation. No CT, WSI, RNA, or WXS native patient-geometry results are available in this round, so cross-modal consistency cannot be re-evaluated here.

biological_support.dimension_interpretation: K3_C0003 shows a coherent and interpretable transcriptomic phenotype relative to the rest of the partition: a coordinated depletion of immune/inflammatory programs (allograft rejection, IL6/JAK/STAT3, interferon alpha and gamma, complement) alongside down-regulated oxidative phosphorylation, proliferation (E2F, G2M), mTORC1, and EMT, with up-regulated TGF-beta, WNT/beta-catenin, and UV-response-DN programs. The strongest enrichments are down-regulated immune hallmarks with fdr_q=0.001 and |NES| up to ~2.10, indicating a substantial and internally consistent molecular program rather than isolated pathway hits. This characterizes biological identity only; it does not establish that current membership, boundary, or granularity deserves independent retention.
biological_support.cross_evidence_context: The WXS report for the complementary set K3_C0001_M_K3_C0002 shows mutation-level differences (e.g., PBRM1 and VHL depletion/enrichment patterns) that, together with this transcriptomic immune-depletion phenotype, describe the two sides of the same reciprocal set-versus-rest contrast. Structural diagnostics for K3_C0003 show a dominant single-cluster resolution (candidate_eigengap 0.9572, screen_candidate_k=1), so the biological phenotype is not accompanied by a screening signal of internal subdivision.
limitations: The partition has exactly two sets, so the set-versus-rest contrasts are reciprocal views of the same comparison, not independent biological confirmations.

confounder_exclusion.dimension_interpretation: At set scope, the same measured technical/acquisition/site factors remain plausible candidate-specific alternative explanations for the membership of K3_C0003 relative to the rest. tissue_source_site (V=0.456, q=0.018), ct_phase (V=0.313, q=0.033), ct_manufacturer (V=0.262, q=0.032), ct_slice_thickness (epsilon^2=0.055, q=0.032), and ct_z_spacing (epsilon^2=0.045, q=0.033) show adjusted associations with membership; ct_pixel_spacing, ct_scanner_model, ct_reconstruction_kernel, and study_year do not. Because the partition has two sets, these associations are the reciprocal mirror of the K3_C0001_M_K3_C0002 screen and are not independent confirmations. These are associations, not causal contributions.
confounder_exclusion.cross_evidence_context: This set-scope screen complements the cross-modal membership geometry for K3_C0003, where CT, RNA, WSI, and WXS all showed positive mean silhouettes (0.088, 0.141, 0.344, 0.185) with low negative fractions in WSI/WXS. The significant CT-related factor associations indicate measured acquisition/site factors remain plausible alternatives even where native-view membership representation is positive; the confounder evidence does not establish that the geometry is technical in origin.
limitations: Association is not causation; significant associations do not prove technical artifact and nonsignificance does not establish absence of confounding.

reports.dimension_interpretation: K3_C0003 shows a coherent and interpretable transcriptomic phenotype relative to the rest of the partition: a coordinated depletion of immune/inflammatory programs (allograft rejection, IL6/JAK/STAT3, interferon alpha and gamma, complement) alongside down-regulated oxidative phosphorylation, proliferation (E2F, G2M), mTORC1, and EMT, with up-regulated TGF-beta, WNT/beta-catenin, and UV-response-DN programs. The strongest enrichments are down-regulated immune hallmarks with fdr_q=0.001 and |NES| up to ~2.10, indicating a substantial and internally consistent molecular program rather than isolated pathway hits. This characterizes biological identity only; it does not establish that current membership, boundary, or granularity deserves independent retention.
reports.cross_evidence_context: The WXS report for the complementary set K3_C0001_M_K3_C0002 shows mutation-level differences (e.g., PBRM1 and VHL depletion/enrichment patterns) that, together with this transcriptomic immune-depletion phenotype, describe the two sides of the same reciprocal set-versus-rest contrast. Structural diagnostics for K3_C0003 show a dominant single-cluster resolution (candidate_eigengap 0.9572, screen_candidate_k=1), so the biological phenotype is not accompanied by a screening signal of internal subdivision.
limitations: The partition has exactly two sets, so the set-versus-rest contrasts are reciprocal views of the same comparison, not independent biological confirmations.
Enrichment is based on the unshrunken DESeq2 Wald-statistic ranking, not adjusted p-values or shrunken fold changes.
fdr_q reflects multiple-testing-adjusted enrichment evidence, not biological importance.
Set size is modest (set_n=28 vs rest_n=75), limiting stability of the ranking.
Biological identity does not by itself establish that current membership, boundary, or granularity deserves independent retention.

reports.dimension_interpretation: Across the four native patient geometries, the current pair boundary between K3_C0001_M_K3_C0002 and K3_C0003 is only weakly represented at best. RNA shows a small positive mean silhouette (0.0619) with 29% negative patients, while CT, WSI, and WXS all show mean silhouettes near zero or slightly negative (CT -0.0049, WSI -0.0090, WXS -0.0045) with substantial negative fractions (CT 51%, WSI 65%, WXS 48%). The within-versus-between distance contrasts are correspondingly minimal in CT, WSI, and WXS. Synthesizing jointly rather than by vote counting, the overall native-view pattern provides weak and largely non-coherent geometric support for the current pair boundary, with RNA the only view showing any positive distinction. This addresses boundary representation only and does not itself determine whether the pair should be merged.
reports.cross_evidence_context: The structural diagnostics for both sets show dominant single-cluster resolutions (candidate_eigengap 0.5724 for K3_C0001_M_K3_C0002 and 0.9572 for K3_C0003, both screen_candidate_k=1), indicating no screening signal of internal subdivision. The biological reports describe a coherent transcriptomic immune-depletion phenotype for K3_C0003 and a weak, non-significant mutation phenotype for K3_C0001_M_K3_C0002, which are reciprocal views of the same two-set contrast.
limitations: Native-view alignments measure current-label representation in each modality geometry and are not votes; strong support in one modality does not override disagreement in others.
The pair boundary evidence does not itself determine whether the pair should be merged.
Silhouette values are descriptive and are not compared against fixed thresholds.

No partition-level GRV or permutation evidence is available in this round.

reports.dimension_interpretation: For K3_C0003, the dominant spectral gap is at the single-cluster resolution (candidate_eigengap 0.9572, screen_candidate_k=1), with subsequent eigengaps much smaller. Feasible k>=2 solutions exist: a two-way split has modest consensus separation (mean silhouette 0.233, balanced children 14/14, normalized cut 0.975) with weakly positive native-view silhouettes except WSI; three- and four-way splits show higher normalized cut and mostly negative native-view silhouettes. Taken together, the screening calculation does not show a dominant internal subdivision signal, and the feasible splits are not corroborated by native-view separation. This weighs against an immediate split hypothesis but is neither positive nor negative evidence about whether the set is independent from neighboring candidates.
reports.cross_evidence_context: The RNA report for this set shows a coherent immune/inflammatory depletion phenotype, and the pair affinity geometry report shows weak and largely non-coherent representation of the boundary between this set and K3_C0001_M_K3_C0002. These are separate evidence roles and do not alter the internal-subdivision interpretation.

reports.dimension_interpretation: In the candidate-generation consensus geometry, the current pair boundary between K3_C0001_M_K3_C0002 and K3_C0003 shows a mixed structural picture. The current boundary is only partially reproduced by an independent two-way spectral partition (ARI 0.581), and the normalized-cut cost is moderate-to-high (0.661), indicating appreciable cross-boundary connectivity rather than clean separation. Within-side affinity (0.428) exceeds between-side affinity (0.228) by roughly a factor of two, so the boundary is the relatively weaker link, but the contrast is moderate. Critically, the union of the two sets is dominated by the single-cluster resolution (candidate_eigengap 0.546 at candidate_k=1, with much smaller subsequent eigengaps), which is merge-compatible evidence and must not be interpreted as support for preserving the current two-set boundary. Taken jointly, the pattern is conflicting-to-weak: a partially represented current boundary coexisting with a single-cluster-dominated union. This is a coherent merge-compatible structural pattern, but it is not by itself sufficient to mandate any action. These are partition-level structural diagnostics only and do not establish biological meaning or clinical validity.
reports.cross_evidence_context: This pair-scope structural screen is consistent with the prior partition-level structural screen, which also found the current boundary to be the relatively weakest link (nearest-pair between-set affinity 0.228, below both within-set values). It is also consistent with the prior affinity-geometry-concordance report, which found only weak and largely non-coherent native-view representation of the current pair boundary (RNA the only view with a small positive mean silhouette, CT/WSI/WXS near zero or slightly negative). The single-cluster-dominated union here aligns with the merge-compatible reading of that weak boundary representation. No CT, WSI, RNA, or WXS native patient-geometry results are available in this round, so cross-modal consistency cannot be re-evaluated here.
limitations: Structural diagnostics are triage evidence and do not by themselves establish biological meaning or clinical validity.
The geometry basis is candidate-generation consensus, not external validation or a stability score.
The union eigengap candidate_k=1 is merge-compatible evidence and must not be read as support for preserving the current two-set boundary.

No CT, WSI, RNA, or WXS native patient-geometry results are available in this round, so cross-modal consistency cannot be evaluated.
This report addresses boundary representation only and does not recommend accept, drop, split, or merge.

reports.dimension_interpretation: At set scope, the same measured technical/acquisition/site factors remain plausible candidate-specific alternative explanations for the membership of K3_C0003 relative to the rest. tissue_source_site (V=0.456, q=0.018), ct_phase (V=0.313, q=0.033), ct_manufacturer (V=0.262, q=0.032), ct_slice_thickness (epsilon^2=0.055, q=0.032), and ct_z_spacing (epsilon^2=0.045, q=0.033) show adjusted associations with membership; ct_pixel_spacing, ct_scanner_model, ct_reconstruction_kernel, and study_year do not. Because the partition has two sets, these associations are the reciprocal mirror of the K3_C0001_M_K3_C0002 screen and are not independent confirmations. These are associations, not causal contributions.
reports.cross_evidence_context: This set-scope screen complements the cross-modal membership geometry for K3_C0003, where CT, RNA, WSI, and WXS all showed positive mean silhouettes (0.088, 0.141, 0.344, 0.185) with low negative fractions in WSI/WXS. The significant CT-related factor associations indicate measured acquisition/site factors remain plausible alternatives even where native-view membership representation is positive; the confounder evidence does not establish that the geometry is technical in origin.
limitations: Association is not causation; significant associations do not prove technical artifact and nonsignificance does not establish absence of confounding.
No covariate adjustment, causal control, or persistence-after-adjustment is demonstrated by this analysis.

reports.dimension_interpretation: Synthesizing the four native geometries jointly, the current membership of K3_C0003 is coherently represented: all four views show positive mean silhouettes with low negative fractions and within distances smaller than between distances, with WSI strongest (0.344) and CT weakest (0.088). The overall native-view pattern provides coherent, though modest in CT and RNA, membership representation. This addresses membership representation only and does not by itself determine accept or drop.
reports.cross_evidence_context: This set-scope membership geometry is consistent with the pair-scope boundary report, which found the pair boundary only weakly represented overall; the positive set-scope silhouettes here reflect that K3_C0003 is the smaller, more compact side of the pair. The set-scope confounder screen for the same target found significant associations with tissue_source_site, ct_phase, ct_manufacturer, ct_slice_thickness, and ct_z_spacing, so measured acquisition/site factors remain plausible alternatives even where representation is positive. Prior structural diagnostics found no dominant internal subdivision signal, which is neither positive nor negative evidence about independence from neighboring candidates.
limitations: Native-view alignments measure current-label representation in each modality geometry and are not votes; strong support in one modality does not override disagreement in others.
Silhouette values are descriptive and are not compared against fixed thresholds.
